Guidance & outlook: The PBDIT has declined from ₹ 7,495.87 Lakhs (FY 2024-25) to ₹ 5,866.56 Lakhs (FY 2025-26).
On a consolidated basis, the Company reported a net loss of ₹3,333 lakhs for FY 2025-26 as compared to a net loss of ₹1,628 lakhs for FY 2024-25.

The PBDIT has declined from ₹7,495.87 Lakhs (FY 2024-2025) to ₹5,866.56 Lakhs (FY 2025-2026) on account of the fact that in FY 2024-25 the profit on sale of land had resulted in higher PBDIT and in the current year Fy2025-26 there was surge in raw material cost and production overhead. .
Growth & demand: Delivering Growth Through Strategic Portfolio Expansion During the year, revenue from operations increased by 11% compared to the previous financial year, reflecting healthy growth in our core businesses and improved topline performance.

New Products in the Pipeline UCAL continues to strengthen its new product pipeline by expanding its electronics and mechatronics development capabilities to address the evolving requirements of the automotive industry.
The Company' s strategic focus on new product development delivered significant results, with revenue from new products increasing by 150% during the year.
Margins & costs: L Thriyambak, Cost Accountant Chennai, as the Cost Auditor to conduct the Cost Audit of the Company for the financial year 2026-27 at a remuneration of ₹ 3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs only) per annum excluding applicable Tax and out of pocket expenses, if any.

THREATS • No or few new developments of Engine platform in IC engines • Competitive pressure on pricing policies. • Rising input cost. • Relentless pressure to reduce prices by OEMs thereby affecting profit margin. • Increased emphasis on electric mobility vehicle 6.

Overall Outcome • Total Power Saved: Approximately 5.0 lakh units for FY 2025-26. • Cost Savings: An estimated reduction of ₹37.50 lakhs in regular electricity expenses. • Cost Savings: An estimated reduction of ₹35.0 lakhs in expenses through strategic solar power purchase.
Capex & expansion: CAPITAL EXPENDITURE (CAPEX) During the year, your Company has spent an amount of `33.97 Crore towards Capex.
For the year 2026-27, the estimated Capex would be around `45 crores towards normal Capex.

3) Limit of Remuneration/Commission: Remuneration/ Commission may be paid within the monetary limit approved by shareholders, subject to the limit not exceeding 1% of the profits of the Company computed as per the applicable provisions of the Act.
Balance sheet & cash: DIVIDEND In order to preserve cash flow for meeting out future capex requirements for various projects to be undertaken by the Company, the Board of Directors has decided to retain the profits and hence no dividend was recommended by the Board of Directors for the financial year 2025-26.

INVESTOR EDUCATION AND PROTECTION FUND (IEPF) • Transfer of Unclaimed Dividends to IEPF, during the year under review: Your Company transferred a sum of ₹ 8,09,170 during the financial year 2025-26 to the Investor Education and Protection Fund established by the Central Government, in compliance with Sections 123 to 125 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Debt Service coverage Ratio % Earnings available for Debt Services / Debt Services (51.13%) 50.72% (101.85) * 4.
Risks & challenges: Global disruptions, including geopolitical uncertainties and volatility in the Middle East region, further contributed to input cost pressures.

The Company has a risk management mechanism in place to manage uncertainties through risk identification, assessment of risk on the scale of probability and severity, risk management framework, risk matrix, risk score, the format of reporting of risk areas and mitigation plan to overcome the risks circulated to all the department heads.
The risks are classified as financial risks, operational risks, market risks and statutory compliance risks.
